To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed novel alkaline anion exchange membranes with varying thicknesses and investigated their performance in single cell fuel cells.
we developed an alkaline anion exchange membrane that can be used for fuel cells at 50 ° C with a non-Pt catalyst at the cathode.

the thinnest ETFE AAEM (S 20) achieved the highest power density of 250 mW cm−2 at 50 ° C in H2/O 2 single cell fuel cell tests, and that the Pt-based catalysts can be replaced by non-precious metal catalysts such as FePc (iron phthalocyanine) for the ORR in alkaline fuel cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials and methods that will improve fuel cell efficiency and performance.
the preparation of novel alkaline anion exchange membranes and non-Polymetallic (non-Pt) cathode catalysts for the oxygen reduction reactions.
the development and testing of novel materials for low temperature fuel cell applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a thin, high ion exchange capacity, low methanol permeability AAEM can be prepared by e-beam irradiating ETFE with quaternary amines.
the thinnest ETFE AAEM (S-20) with the highest ionic conductivity and lowest methanol crossover was the most suitable membrane for low temperature alkaline fuel cells.
this thesis has shown that ETFE AAEMs can be used in H2/Oxidation fuel cells at low temperatures and non-Pt electro-catalysts can also be used in the cathode of the fuel cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pt/C catalysts are still the best catalysts for ORR in alkaline fuel cells, but that the performance of the non-Pt catalyst can be improved by increasing the surface area of the carbon support.
the thinnest ETFE-AAEM (S20), with a thickness of 20 µm, showed the best performance.
the use of the thinnest ETFE-AAEM (S20), in conjunction with a non-Pt catalyst, is the best combination to obtain the highest performance at 50 ° C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a thinner membrane (S20) with non-Pt catalyst (Pd) can achieve a power density of 180 mW cm−2.
the ORR performance of the non-Pt electro-catalysts is not only highly dependent on the catalyst composition but also on the membrane used.
a thin AAEM is preferred to achieve higher fuel cell performance.
